candidate.title: ToggleVirtualDisplay has no per-permission authorization check — any non-view_camera peer can plug in/out virtual monitors
candidate.component: virtual-display toggle (misc dispatch -> virtual_display_manager -> virtual_display crate)
candidate.root_cause: toggle_virtual_display() in connection.rs (invoked from the Misc dispatch at connection.rs:3452 guarded only by `if !self.view_camera`) never calls Self::permission(...) before invoking virtual_display_manager::plug_in_monitor/plug_out_monitor, unlike every sibling privileged action in the same match block: RestartRemoteDevice checks self.restart (connection.rs:3496-3499), change_resolution checks self.keyboard (connection.rs:4310-4311), turn_on_privacy checks self.privacy_mode (connection.rs:4649). There is also no Permission::virtual_display variant in the rendezvous_proto control_permissions enum used by Self::permission() (connection.rs:2388-2415, enumerates keyboard/remote_printer/clipboard/file/audio/camera/terminal/tunnel/restart/recording/block_input/privacy_mode only), so under RustDesk Pro/Enterprise fine-grained address-book roles this action can never be individually restricted at all.
candidate.entry_point: Malicious/authenticated CONTROLLER sends a Misc{ToggleVirtualDisplay{on, display}} protobuf message over an established (non-view_camera) session — connection.rs:3450-3455.
candidate.sink: virtual_display_manager::plug_in_monitor()/plug_out_monitor() (src/virtual_display_manager.rs:72-93), which for IDD_IMPL_RUSTDESK builds calls virtual_display::plug_in_monitor()/plug_out_monitor() in the target crate /Users/krasn/tools/raptor/targets/rustdesk/libs/virtual_display/src/lib.rs:160-186 (native FFI into dylib_virtual_display / RustDeskIddDriver), and for the currently-selected IDD_IMPL_AMYUNI build calls amyuni_idd::plug_in_monitor()/plug_out_monitor() (src/virtual_display_manager.rs:647-700, a real IOCTL device_io_control to the amyuni virtual-display kernel driver).
candidate.trace: connection.rs:3452 dispatch (`if !self.view_camera`) -> connection.rs:4260 toggle_virtual_display() (no Self::permission check) -> connection.rs:4279 virtual_display_manager::plug_in_monitor(t.display as _, Vec::new()) / connection.rs:4290 virtual_display_manager::plug_out_monitor(t.display, false, true) -> src/virtual_display_manager.rs:72-93 top-level dispatch -> (IDD_RUSTDESK) libs/virtual_display/src/lib.rs plug_in_monitor/plug_out_monitor native call, or (IDD_AMYUNI, default) amyuni_idd device_io_control.
candidate.attack: A controller connects with a session where every individual permission (keyboard, file, clipboard, audio, camera, terminal, tunnel, restart, recording, block_input, privacy_mode) is denied by the host's fine-grained role (Pro/Enterprise control_permissions), i.e. a 'view + chat only' style grant. Attacker sends Misc{toggle_virtual_display{on:true, display:1}} then Misc{toggle_virtual_display{on:false, display:1}} repeatedly. Because the dispatch only checks `!self.view_camera` (true for any non-view-camera-only auth type) and toggle_virtual_display() never calls Self::permission(), the server plugs in/out virtual monitors on the host regardless of the granted permission set, letting a controller with essentially no control rights still manipulate the host's display topology (add/remove monitors up to the 4/5-monitor cap) and disrupt the session.
candidate.confidence_reason: Directly confirmed by reading the dispatch and handler code and comparing to three sibling handlers that DO check a permission flag in the identical match block; no Permission::virtual_display enum variant exists to gate it even in the fine-grained model. Severity is capped because worst-observed concrete effect in the current default build (amyuni_idd) is bounded monitor add/remove, not memory corruption.
candidate.disposition_hint: review-for-validation

verdict.reason:
Fully verified against raw source, no refutation found.

1. Dispatch (connection.rs:3451-3455, `#[cfg(windows)]`-gated): `Some(misc::Union::ToggleVirtualDisplay(t)) => { if !self.view_camera { self.toggle_virtual_display(t).await; } }`. `self.view_camera` is set true ONLY for the narrow login_request::Union::ViewCamera session type (connection.rs:2551, itself gated on OPTION_ENABLE_CAMERA permission at login, connection.rs:2547-2552) and reset to false for every normal session (connection.rs:2443, reset_session_scope_for_login). So `!self.view_camera` is true for essentially every ordinary remote-control session regardless of which individual permissions were granted.

2. toggle_virtual_display() (connection.rs:4260-4299) confirmed read in full: only checks `virtual_display_manager::is_virtual_display_supported()` (an OS-version capability check, not an authorization check) before calling `plug_in_monitor`/`plug_out_monitor` directly. No `Self::permission(...)` call, no `self.<flag>` gate anywhere in the function.

3. Verified by contrast: sibling handlers in the identical match block DO gate on a permission-derived struct field — `self.restart` (connection.rs:3498, RestartRemoteDevice), `self.keyboard` (connection.rs:4311, change_resolution), `self.privacy_mode`/`is_authed_remote_conn` (connection.rs:4649, turn_on_privacy). These fields are all populated at connection construction directly from `Self::permission(keys::OPTION_ENABLE_*, &control_permissions)` (connection.rs:520-528), which reads `ControlPermissions.Permission` — confirmed in libs/hbb_common/protos/rendezvous.proto:33-49 to contain exactly 13 variants (keyboard, remote_printer, clipboard, file, audio, camera, terminal, tunnel, restart, recording, block_input, remote_modify, privacy_mode) and NO `virtual_display` variant. So even under RustDesk Pro/Enterprise's fine-grained per-permission model, there is no way to gate this action at all — it structurally cannot be denied.

4. Sink chain confirmed live and consequential, not a stub: virtual_display_manager::plug_in_monitor/plug_out_monitor (virtual_display_manager.rs:72-93) dispatch to `amyuni_idd::plug_in_monitor()`/`plug_out_monitor()` (the compiled-in default, `const IDD_IMPL: &str = IDD_IMPL_AMYUNI`, virtual_display_manager.rs:9), which perform a real `win_device::device_io_control` IOCTL (virtual_display_manager.rs:543) against the amyuni virtual-display driver, bounded by `VIRTUAL_DISPLAY_MAX_COUNT` = 4 (amyuni, line 413) / 5 (rustdesk_idd, line 142) — exactly matching the candidate's "4/5-monitor cap" claim.

Only correction to the candidate text: the control_permissions enum actually has 13 variants including `remote_modify`, which the candidate's list omitted (said "...tunnel/restart/recording/block_input/privacy_mode only" — missing remote_modify) — a trivial completeness slip that doesn't affect the core claim (virtual_display is still absent either way). Also worth noting for scope precision: the vulnerable dispatch arm is `#[cfg(windows)]`-gated (Windows hosts only), which the candidate's trace/sink description already makes clear via the Windows-only driver stack, so this isn't a new fact, just confirms scope. Severity as rated (Medium, capped by "bounded monitor add/remove, not memory corruption" under the default amyuni build) is accurate and appropriately conservative — not over- or under-rated.

candidate.title: virtual_display::plug_in_monitor / plug_out_monitor forward an unvalidated u32 monitor index straight into the native/kernel IDD driver call with no range check
candidate.root_cause: plug_in_monitor(monitor_index: u32) (lib.rs:161-174) only checks whether monitor_index is already present in the de-dup set MONITOR_INDICES (lib.rs:163-165); it never bounds-checks monitor_index against any driver-imposed maximum before calling the native exported function `f(monitor_index, 0, 20)` at lib.rs:171. plug_out_monitor(monitor_index: u32) (lib.rs:177-186) has no membership check at all and unconditionally forwards monitor_index straight to the native call `f(monitor_index)` at lib.rs:183 before touching MONITOR_INDICES. update_monitor_modes() (lib.rs:189-196) likewise forwards `monitor_index` unchecked. These are the only validation gates before the value crosses the Rust/native FFI boundary into the RustDeskIddDriver's exported PlugInMonitor/PlugOutMonitor/UpdateMonitorModes entry points (implemented in libs/virtual_display/dylib, an indirect-display kernel-mode driver reached via IOCTL).
candidate.entry_point: Any caller of the public virtual_display crate API with an out-of-range or attacker-influenced u32 index; concretely, src/virtual_display_manager.rs's rustdesk_idd::plug_in_index_modes(idx, modes) (src/virtual_display_manager.rs:257) passes the caller-supplied idx straight through with only a HashMap containment check (`!manager.peer_index_name.contains_key(&idx)`, no upper bound), and that idx is itself sourced (when IDD_IMPL_RUSTDESK is selected) from the network-controlled Misc.ToggleVirtualDisplay.display field (connection.rs:4279, `t.display as _`) with zero range validation anywhere in the chain.
candidate.sink: Native/kernel call into dylib_virtual_display's exported PlugInMonitor/PlugOutMonitor/UpdateMonitorModes (RustDeskIddDriver), lib.rs:161-196.
candidate.trace: connection.rs:4279 t.display(i32, attacker-controlled) as u32 -> src/virtual_display_manager.rs:72-75 plug_in_monitor(idx, modes) -> (IDD_IMPL_RUSTDESK) src/virtual_display_manager.rs:257 rustdesk_idd::plug_in_index_modes(idx, modes) -> src/virtual_display_manager.rs:177-178 VirtualDisplayManager::plug_in_monitor(index, modes) -> libs/virtual_display/src/lib.rs:161-174 virtual_display::plug_in_monitor(monitor_index) -> native FFI call f(monitor_index, 0, 20) into the IDD kernel driver, with monitor_index never range-checked at any layer.
candidate.attack: With IDD_IMPL set to "rustdesk_idd" (a real, actively-referenced implementation still wired into change_resolution_if_is_virtual_display and is_virtual_display, currently gated off only by the single hardcoded `const IDD_IMPL: &str = IDD_IMPL_AMYUNI;` in src/virtual_display_manager.rs:8), a controller sends Misc{toggle_virtual_display{on:true, display:0x7FFFFFFF}} (or any large/unexpected 32-bit value). The value crosses unchecked into the driver's PlugInMonitor(index,...) exported function, which — depending on how the C/kernel driver indexes its internal monitor table (see libs/virtual_display/dylib/src/win10/IddController.c, out of this slice's file set) — may read/write out of bounds of a fixed-size internal array, causing a kernel-mode indirect-display-driver crash or, if the driver trusts the index for a table write, potential memory corruption in driver context.
candidate.preconditions: Requires the build to select IDD_IMPL_RUSTDESK (not the current default IDD_IMPL_AMYUNI in this snapshot — under the current build this exact chain is compiled but unreachable at runtime from the network entry point, since the match at src/virtual_display_manager.rs:74-75 always takes the AMYUNI arm). Also requires whatever bound-checking (or lack thereof) exists in the native IddController.c driver, which is outside the 4 files reviewed here.
candidate.confidence_reason: The missing bounds check in the target file's own public API (lib.rs) is directly confirmed by reading the code — it is a genuine defense-in-depth gap in a driver-facing wrapper. However, the concrete network-reachable exploit chain is dead code in the currently-selected IDD_IMPL_AMYUNI build (confirmed via grep: rustdesk_idd::plug_in_index_modes is only called from the IDD_IMPL-gated dispatch, never directly), and actual memory-safety impact depends on native driver code not in this file set, so this is reported primarily as an unvalidated-input-into-privileged-driver-call code defect rather than a proven live RCE/DoS path.
candidate.disposition_hint: needs-further-investigation

verdict.reason: Read lib.rs directly: plug_in_monitor (161-174) only dedupes via MONITOR_INDICES, no range check, before calling native f(monitor_index,0,20); plug_out_monitor (177-186) and update_monitor_modes (189-196) forward monitor_index with zero checks. That part of the claim is accurate. But the reachability chain is not merely 'currently unselected config' -- it is structurally dead code with no runtime or build-time switch. src/virtual_display_manager.rs:8 declares `const IDD_IMPL: &str = IDD_IMPL_AMYUNI;` and a full-repo grep for IDD_IMPL (rs+toml, excluding target/) turns up only its 3 definition lines and its read-sites inside virtual_display_manager.rs -- no Cargo feature, no env var, no config file, no cfg() gate anywhere touches it. Every call into the vulnerable virtual_display::plug_in_monitor/plug_out_monitor/update_monitor_modes functions goes through rustdesk_idd::plug_in_index_modes/plug_in_headless/plug_out_headless (virtual_display_manager.rs:161-234), and those in turn are reachable ONLY from the `match IDD_IMPL { IDD_IMPL_RUSTDESK => ..., IDD_IMPL_AMYUNI => ... }` dispatch (lines 37-38, 73-75, 81-90, 96-97, 111-112, 124-126) which always takes the AMYUNI arm at both compile-observed and runtime-observed level (it's a plain string-const match, not a cfg feature -- there is no build variant of this exact source tree where it takes the other arm). I additionally checked the other public rustdesk_idd functions reachable from outside the module (core_main.rs:291 install_update_driver, display_service.rs:259 is_virtual_display, connection.rs:4318 change_resolution_if_is_virtual_display) -- all three only read VIRTUAL_DISPLAY_MANAGER's peer_index_name/headless_index_name maps, which are populated exclusively by plug_in_index_modes/plug_in_headless, i.e. they are provably always-empty in the shipped binary, so those call sites are inert no-ops too. connection.rs:4279's Misc.ToggleVirtualDisplay handler (gated only by `!self.view_camera`, confirmed at connection.rs:3451-3454) does reach virtual_display_manager::plug_in_monitor with the attacker-controlled t.display value, but that function's IDD_IMPL match (line 73-75) discards the rustdesk_idd arm entirely at runtime and calls amyuni_idd::plug_in_monitor() instead, which never touches libs/virtual_display/src/lib.rs -- amyuni_idd uses a completely separate win_device/plug_monitor_ mechanism (virtual_display_manager.rs ~560-650) with no relation to the file under review. So the candidate's own hedge ('unreachable at runtime... under the current build') actually understates the finding: this isn't config-dependent unreachability, it's zero-switch dead code -- reaching it requires editing RustDesk's own Rust source (flipping one const) and recompiling, which is outside any attacker or even operator/deployer capability. That is a stronger and more definitive form of non-reachability than 'Low' severity implies (Low still connotes some residual live exposure under realistic deployment variance); it merits Informational -- a genuine defense-in-depth code defect worth fixing, with zero live exploitability in the shipped/compiled RustDesk product as it stands in this source tree.
verdict.corrected_root_cause: Confirmed as stated: virtual_display::plug_in_monitor/plug_out_monitor/update_monitor_modes (lib.rs:161-196) forward an attacker-influenceable u32 monitor_index into the native IDD driver FFI call with no upper-bound validation (only a dedup/membership check in plug_in_monitor, none at all in the other two). This is a real, provable gap in the wrapper's own input validation.
verdict.observed_mitigation: src/virtual_display_manager.rs:8 `const IDD_IMPL: &str = IDD_IMPL_AMYUNI;` is the sole definition of IDD_IMPL in the entire repo (verified via grep across *.rs/*.toml excluding target/) -- no Cargo feature flag, cfg(), or env var switches it. Every caller of the vulnerable lib.rs functions is gated behind `match IDD_IMPL { IDD_IMPL_RUSTDESK => ..., IDD_IMPL_AMYUNI => ... }` (virtual_display_manager.rs:37-38,73-75,81-90,96-97,111-112,124-126), which always takes the AMYUNI arm; the AMYUNI arm's own plug_in_monitor()/plug_out_monitor() implementation (virtual_display_manager.rs ~560-680) is a wholly separate windows-device-manager path (win_device/plug_monitor_) that never calls into libs/virtual_display/src/lib.rs. The network-reachable entry point connection.rs:4279 (Misc.ToggleVirtualDisplay, gated only by `!self.view_camera`) therefore never exercises the unchecked code, confirmed by tracing its call through virtual_display_manager::plug_in_monitor -> the IDD_IMPL match -> amyuni_idd::plug_in_monitor(), bypassing rustdesk_idd/lib.rs entirely.
verdict.live_test: Not required for the reachability question -- the gate is a hardcoded Rust const with no external toggle, so no test harness or network probe against the shipped binary can reach the rustdesk_idd/lib.rs code path; this is a static/structural proof, not a probabilistic one. If IDD_IMPL were ever flipped to IDD_IMPL_RUSTDESK in a future build, live validation would then be needed against the actual RustDeskIddDriver kernel driver (out-of-repo, libs/virtual_display/dylib) to determine whether an out-of-range monitor_index causes an OOB array write/kernel crash or is itself bounds-checked driver-side -- that native code was not available to review.

candidate.title: Printer driver install path is resolved from current_exe()'s parent directory with no integrity check — local-write-then-install pattern if the running binary is not in an admin-protected directory
candidate.root_cause: get_driver_inf_abs_path() (setup.rs:14-32) builds the INF path used for printer-driver installation purely from `std::env::current_exe()?.parent()` joined with the hardcoded constant RD_DRIVER_INF_PATH ("drivers/RustDeskPrinterDriver/RustDeskPrinterDriver.inf", lib.rs:10), with only an existence check (`abs_path.exists()`, setup.rs:25) and no signature/hash/ACL verification of either the INF or the driver package files it references. install_update_printer() (setup.rs:44-79) then feeds this path straight into install_driver() (driver.rs:152-202), which calls UploadPrinterDriverPackageW/InstallPrinterDriverFromPackageW (driver.rs:156-199) to install the referenced driver package into the system driver store. If the RustDesk executable is ever run from a directory writable by a lower-privileged principal than the process performing the install (e.g., a portable/self-extracted deployment run from a user-writable folder, later invoked with elevated/service rights), an attacker who can write to that directory can substitute their own RustDeskPrinterDriver.inf + package before install_update_printer() runs, causing the elevated process to install an attacker-supplied printer driver package.
candidate.entry_point: Local attacker with write access to the RustDesk executable's directory (e.g., portable build under a user-writable path) plants a malicious drivers/RustDeskPrinterDriver/RustDeskPrinterDriver.inf (plus referenced driver files) before install_update_printer() is triggered (via --install-remote-printer CLI flag in core_main.rs:308-320, or main_set_common("install-printer") in flutter_ffi.rs:2905-2906).
candidate.sink: install_driver() -> UploadPrinterDriverPackageW/InstallPrinterDriverFromPackageW, driver.rs:152-202.
candidate.trace: core_main.rs:311 / flutter_ffi.rs:2906 remote_printer::install_update_printer(app_name) -> setup.rs:52 get_driver_inf_abs_path() (trusts current_exe() parent dir blindly) -> setup.rs:73 install_driver(&rd_printer_driver_name, inf_file.as_ptr()) -> driver.rs:156-199 UploadPrinterDriverPackageW/InstallPrinterDriverFromPackageW using the untrusted inf path.
candidate.attack: On a portable/unpacked-to-user-writable-directory deployment, a local non-admin attacker replaces drivers/RustDeskPrinterDriver/RustDeskPrinterDriver.inf and the referenced driver binaries in the RustDesk app directory with a malicious print-driver package, then either waits for the legitimate user/service to trigger printer install, or triggers it themselves via the --install-remote-printer CLI flag or the 'enable remote printer' UI toggle. If that install runs with higher privilege than the attacker (e.g., triggered while running elevated, or the directory is briefly writable during setup), the attacker's driver package gets installed into the Windows driver store and loaded into the (SYSTEM-privileged) Print Spooler process, yielding code execution as SYSTEM/spooler.
candidate.preconditions: Requires (a) the RustDesk executable to be running from a directory writable by a principal less privileged than the process performing the install, and (b) install_update_printer() to actually execute with elevated privileges relative to that writer — neither is confirmed from the 4 files in this slice alone (the IPC/elevation call sites that invoke this are outside the assigned file set), so this is reported as a plausible local-write-then-install pattern rather than a proven exploit chain.
candidate.confidence_reason: The missing integrity check on the exe-relative INF path is directly confirmed in setup.rs. However, whether the process ever actually runs elevated/as-SYSTEM relative to a user-writable install directory is speculative — the IPC/elevation plumbing that would establish that precondition lives outside the four target files, and normal (non-portable) RustDesk installs place the exe under an admin-only Program Files directory where this is not exploitable.
candidate.disposition_hint: needs-further-investigation

verdict.reason:
setup.rs:14-31 is exactly as claimed: get_driver_inf_abs_path() builds the INF path from std::env::current_exe()?.parent().join(RD_DRIVER_INF_PATH) with only an .exists() check (line 25) — no signature, hash, or ACL verification of the INF or the driver package it references. install_update_printer() (setup.rs:44-79) feeds that path into install_driver() (driver.rs:152-202), which calls UploadPrinterDriverPackageW/InstallPrinterDriverFromPackageW — confirmed, no mitigating check anywhere in these files. I could not refute the root cause; I could only sharpen/attenuate the reachability precondition, which the candidate itself flagged as unconfirmed.

New evidence found outside the 4 assigned files that changes the picture: src/platform/windows.rs:1671 captures `src_exe = std::env::current_exe()?` — the CURRENTLY RUNNING (pre-copy) installer exe path — and at line 1692 builds `"{src_exe}" --install-remote-printer` into the install batch script, which is executed via `runas::Command::new("cmd.exe").force_prompt(true)` (windows.rs:1900-1904, a UAC-elevation prompt) at windows.rs:1747. Critically this happens BEFORE any reference to the post-install Program-Files copy in the script — i.e. the standard (non-portable) installer's elevated printer-driver-install step reads the INF/package from wherever the installer .exe was originally launched from (e.g. Downloads/temp/a shared staging dir), not from the hardened install directory. This directly contradicts the candidate's own caveat that 'normal (non-portable) RustDesk installs place the exe under an admin-only Program Files directory where this is not exploitable' — the vulnerable lookup fires on the pre-install location for ALL installs with the printer option enabled (windows.rs:1645-1646, gated by `options.contains(\"printer\")`), not just portable builds. Also independently reachable via `--install-remote-printer` CLI (core_main.rs:308-320) and the `install-printer` FFI/UI action (flutter_ffi.rs:2904-2906), neither of which is proven-elevation from these files alone.

What remains genuinely unobservable from source and requires a live Windows test: (1) whether UploadPrinterDriverPackageW's silent path (UPDP_SILENT_UPLOAD, driver.rs:156-164) actually accepts an unsigned/attacker-crafted driver package on a default Windows 10/11 config, or whether Windows driver-signing/Point-and-Print policy blocks it and falls back to the UI-consent path (driver.rs:171-179, GetForegroundWindow prompt) — that fallback would require an explicit human click and meaningfully reduce silent-exploitability; (2) whether real RustDesk deployment/staging practice (self-download to per-user Downloads vs. enterprise RMM/SCCM push to a shared/world-writable staging path) ever creates the needed differential-privilege condition (writer principal ≠ elevating principal). Absent that, a single user elevating their own downloaded installer via UAC is not a privilege boundary crossing.
verdict.corrected_root_cause: Confirmed as originally stated, and reachability is stronger than the candidate could establish from the 4 assigned files: the standard (non-portable) Windows installer flow itself (windows.rs:1671-1747, install_printer feature gated at windows.rs:1645) invokes the vulnerable current_exe()-relative INF lookup under UAC elevation using the PRE-install exe location, not just a hypothetical 'portable build in a bad directory' edge case.
verdict.corrected_severity: Medium (up from candidate's Low) — root cause and elevated-reachability are code-confirmed; full exploitability still gated by an environment fact (writable staging dir + a lower-priv writer distinct from the elevating principal) and a Windows-OS behavior (silent vs. UI-gated untrusted-driver install) that cannot be resolved from source.
verdict.observed_mitigation: None present in the 4 target files (setup.rs/driver.rs) — no signature/hash/ACL check anywhere on the resolved INF path. The only potential mitigation is external to this code: Windows' own driver-package trust enforcement inside UploadPrinterDriverPackageW, which falls back from a silent install attempt (driver.rs:156-164, UPDP_SILENT_UPLOAD) to a UI-consent prompt (driver.rs:171-179) on failure — this is an OS-level behavior, not a check written by RustDesk, and its actual effect on an attacker-supplied unsigned/self-signed package is unverified from source.
verdict.live_test: On a Windows 10/11 VM: (1) build/install RustDesk with the printer option, stage the installer .exe in a directory ACL'd writable by a low-priv standard user (simulating a shared/RMM staging path e.g. C:\Windows\Temp or C:\Users\Public), (2) as the low-priv user, overwrite drivers/RustDeskPrinterDriver/RustDeskPrinterDriver.inf and its referenced package files with a malicious/test printer driver package (unsigned first, then attacker-controlled-signed), (3) as an admin/elevated principal, run the installer from that same staged path with the printer option enabled and accept the UAC prompt, (4) observe whether UploadPrinterDriverPackageW/InstallPrinterDriverFromPackageW installs the substituted package silently or requires an explicit UI click, and whether the installed driver DLL loads into the SYSTEM-privileged spoolsv.exe process. A silent, no-click install of the substituted package would confirm SYSTEM-level local privilege escalation from a shared-staging-directory write primitive.

candidate.title: show_my_cursor whiteboard broadcast is self-granted by the controller with no host-consent check, unlike every sibling permission
candidate.root_cause: update_options() in connection.rs does not check self.keyboard / peer_keyboard_enabled() (or any host-granted permission flag) before honoring OptionMessage.show_my_cursor, unlike the immediately preceding block_input handler (line ~4453: 'if self.keyboard && self.block_input') which explicitly gates on the keyboard permission. Any connection whose AuthConnType is Remote (which covers both full-control AND view-only screen-share sessions -- the distinction is only the runtime self.keyboard flag, not the conn type) can set self.show_my_cursor = true purely by sending an OptionMessage, with zero host-side approval, and self.show_my_cursor is never reset when keyboard/control permission is later revoked (grep confirms it is only ever assigned at connection.rs:4606).
candidate.entry_point: Malicious/curious CONTROLLER (authenticated at any permission tier, including a view-only 'screen share' grant with self.keyboard=false) sends Misc.Option{show_my_cursor: Yes} over an already-authorized session.
candidate.sink: whiteboard::update_whiteboard() in /Users/krasn/tools/raptor/targets/rustdesk/src/whiteboard/client.rs:84 -> tx_send_event() (client.rs:124) -> IPC Data::Whiteboard send to the spawned whiteboard renderer process -> whiteboard/server.rs:handle_new_stream (line 89) forwards the event to EVENT_PROXY, which drives the OS-native rendering loop (windows.rs/macos.rs/linux.rs, confirmed via draw_text(&cursor.text,...) call sites) that paints a moving, labeled cursor overlay directly on the HOST's own screen.
candidate.trace: connection.rs:4603-4629 update_options() sets self.show_my_cursor=true and calls whiteboard::register_whiteboard(get_key_cursor(conn_id)) with no permission check -> connection.rs:2866 'else if self.show_my_cursor' branch in the MouseEvent handler: even when self.peer_keyboard_enabled()==false, every subsequent MouseEvent from this same connection is still passed to self.input_mouse(..., simulate=false, show_cursor=true) -> input_service.rs handle_mouse_() calls handle_mouse_show_cursor_(evt, conn, username=self.lr.my_name (attacker-controlled string), argb=self.peer_argb) -> whiteboard::update_whiteboard() (client.rs:84) queues a CustomEvent::Cursor{x,y,argb,btns,text=username} -> forwarded over the whiteboard IPC channel to the renderer process which draws the cursor + attacker-controlled name label on the host's live desktop.
candidate.attack: Attacker connects with a view-only/screen-share-only grant (no keyboard/mouse control permission ever given by the host). Attacker sends Misc.Option{show_my_cursor: BoolOption::Yes}, then floods MouseEvent messages with arbitrary x/y coordinates.
